title.zh: 卷一百七十三 列傳第九十八 裴度
title.raw: 卷一百七十三 列傳第九十八 裴度 Volume 173 Biographies 98: Pei Du

sentences.zh: 裴度子:識 諗

translations.literal: Pei Du's sons: Shi and Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du's sons were Shi and Shen.

sentences.zh: 裴度，字中立，河東聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Du, taboo name Zhongli, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du, styled Zhongli, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，擢進士第，以宏辭補校書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, he was elevated to jinshi rank, and through hongci was supplemented as collating secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhenyuan reign he passed the jinshi examination and, through the literary excellence test, was appointed collating secretary.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正異等，調河陰尉。

translations.literal: He was nominated as exceptionally qualified in the Filial and Incorrupt, Upright and Learned category, and was transferred to be magistrate of Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as outstanding in the Filial and Incorrupt, Upright and Learned examination, he was assigned as magistrate of Heyin.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，論權嬖梗切，出為河南功曹參軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to investigating censor; in discussing powerful favorites he was blunt and cutting, and was sent out as staff officer of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to investigating censor, he spoke sharply against powerful favorites at court and was transferred to serve as staff officer in Henan.

sentences.zh: 武元衡帥西川，表掌節度府書記。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanheng commanded Xichuan, he memorialized that Du should manage the secretariat of the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanheng took command of Xichuan, he recommended Du to head the secretariat of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 召為起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be attendant of the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as attendant of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，以司封員外郎知制誥。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe, as outer vice director of the Ministry of Rites for enfeoffments he was put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In 811, as outer vice director in the Ministry of Rites for enfeoffments, he was assigned to draft imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 田弘正效魏、博六州於朝，憲宗遣度宣諭，弘正知度為帝高選，故郊迎趨跽受命，且請遍至屬州，布揚天子德澤，魏人由是歡服。

translations.literal: Tian Hongzheng presented the six prefectures of Wei and Bo to the court; Xianzong sent Du to proclaim and instruct. Hongzheng knew Du was the emperor's high choice, so he went out to the suburbs to welcome him, hurried forward kneeling to receive the mandate, and also requested that he go everywhere to the subordinate prefectures to spread and display the Son of Heaven's virtue and grace; the people of Wei thereby rejoiced and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hongzheng surrendered the six Wei and Bo prefectures to the throne, Emperor Xianzong dispatched Du to announce the imperial will. Knowing that Du was the emperor's chosen envoy, Hongzheng met him outside the city, knelt to receive his instructions, and asked him to visit every subordinate prefecture to proclaim the Son of Heaven's grace. The people of Wei thereupon accepted the new order with relief.

sentences.zh: 還，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: On his return, he was appointed Central Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned, he was appointed a drafter in the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 久之，進御史中丞。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was advanced to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 宣徽五坊小使方秋閱鷹狗，所過撓官司，厚得餉謝乃去。

translations.literal: The petty envoys of the Xuanhui Five Wards were just then in autumn reviewing hawks and dogs; wherever they passed they harassed official business, and only after receiving generous gifts and thanks would they leave.
translations.idiomatic: Petty agents from the Xuanhui Five Wards were touring the autumn falconry circuit, bullying local officials wherever they went and departing only after they had been paid off handsomely.

sentences.zh: 下邽令裴寰，才吏也，不為禮，因構寰出醜言，送詔獄，當大不恭。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Xiagui, Pei Huan, was a talented official; he did not show them courtesy. They therefore framed Huan for uttering ugly words, sent him to the imperial prison, and charged him with grave irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Huan, magistrate of Xiagui, was a capable administrator who refused to defer to them. They fabricated charges that he had spoken slanderously, had him thrown into the imperial prison, and sought the death penalty for grave irreverence.

sentences.zh: 宰相武元衡婉辭諍，帝怒未置。

translations.literal: The chief minister Wu Yuanheng remonstrated in mild words; the emperor was angry and did not release him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Wu Yuanheng pleaded gently on Huan's behalf, but the emperor was furious and would not relent.

sentences.zh: 度見延英，言寰無辜，帝恚曰：「寰誠無罪，杖小使；

translations.literal: Du had an audience at Yanying and said Huan was innocent. The emperor said in anger: "If Huan is truly without guilt, then beat the petty envoy;
translations.idiomatic: Du appeared before the emperor in the Yanying Hall and argued that Huan was innocent. The emperor snapped, "If Huan truly did no wrong, then flog the petty envoy;

sentences.zh: 小使無罪，且杖寰。

translations.literal: if the petty envoy is without guilt, then also beat Huan."
translations.idiomatic: if the envoy did no wrong, then flog Huan as well."

sentences.zh: 」度曰：「責若此固宜，第寰為令，惜陛下百姓，安可罪？

translations.literal: Du said: "If blame is apportioned thus it is indeed fitting; only Huan is a magistrate who cherishes Your Majesty's common people—how can he be punished?"
translations.idiomatic: Du replied, "That would be fair enough in the abstract, but Huan is a magistrate who was protecting Your Majesty's people. How can he be punished for that?"

sentences.zh: 」帝色霽，乃釋寰。

translations.literal: The emperor's expression cleared, and he then released Huan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression softened, and he released Huan.

sentences.zh: 王師討蔡，以度視行營諸軍，還，奏攻取策，與帝意合。

translations.literal: The imperial army was campaigning against Cai; Du was sent to inspect the various armies of the field headquarters. On his return he memorialized strategies for attack and seizure, which matched the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: While the court's armies campaigned against Cai, Du was sent to inspect the forces at headquarters. On his return he submitted a plan of attack that matched the emperor's own thinking.

sentences.zh: 且問諸將才否，度對：「李光顏義而勇，當有成功。

translations.literal: The emperor also asked whether the generals had talent or not. Du replied: "Li Guangyan is righteous and brave; he ought to achieve success."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also asked which commanders were capable. Du answered, "Li Guangyan is loyal and brave; he will succeed."

sentences.zh: 」不三日，光顏破時曲兵，帝歎度知言。

translations.literal: Within three days Guangyan defeated the Shiqu troops, and the emperor sighed that Du knew how to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Within three days Guangyan routed the enemy at Shiqu, and the emperor marveled that Du had judged so rightly.

sentences.zh: 進兼刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced and concurrently made vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted and also appointed vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 王承宗、李師道謀緩蔡兵，乃伏盜京師，刺用事大臣，已害宰相元衡，又擊度，刃三進，斷靴，刜背裂中單，又傷首，度冒氈，得不死。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong and Li Shidao plotted to slacken the Cai campaign, and therefore planted assassins in the capital to stab the powerful ministers. They had already killed Chief Minister Wu Yuanheng, and again struck Du: the blade advanced three times, severed his boot, slashed his back and split his middle garment, and also wounded his head. Du wore a felt cloak and did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong and Li Shidao, hoping to ease pressure on Cai, planted assassins in the capital to kill leading ministers. They had already murdered Chief Minister Wu Yuanheng and now attacked Du. The blade struck three times, cutting through his boot, slashing his back and tearing his under-robe, and wounding his head. Du survived only because he was wearing a thick felt cloak.

sentences.zh: 哄導駭伏，獨騶王義持賊大呼，賊斷義手。

translations.literal: The hubbub and guides fell in terror and prostrated themselves; only his groom Wang Yi seized the assassin and shouted; the assassin severed Yi's hand.
translations.idiomatic: His escort scattered in panic, but his groom Wang Yi alone seized the assassin and shouted for help. The assassin cut off Wang Yi's hand.

sentences.zh: 度墜溝，賊意已死，因亡去。

translations.literal: Du fell into a ditch; the assassin thought he was already dead and therefore fled.
translations.idiomatic: Du fell into a ditch. Believing him dead, the assassin fled.

sentences.zh: 議者欲罷度，安二鎮反側，帝怒曰：「度得全，天也！

translations.literal: Those in council wished to remove Du to reassure the two circuits' wavering loyalty. The emperor said in anger: "That Du survived whole is Heaven's doing!
translations.idiomatic: Some advisers urged removing Du to placate the two rebellious circuits. The emperor thundered, "That Du survived at all was heaven's doing!

sentences.zh: 若罷之，是賊計適行。

translations.literal: If we remove him, the rebels' plan will have succeeded exactly."
translations.idiomatic: If I dismiss him now, the rebels' scheme will have succeeded."

sentences.zh: 吾倚度，足破三賊矣！

translations.literal: I rely on Du—enough to break the three rebels!"
translations.idiomatic: With Du at my side I have men enough to crush all three rebels!"

sentences.zh: 」度亦以權紀未張，王室陵遲，常憤愧無死所。

translations.literal: Du also, because authority and discipline were not extended and the royal house was in decline, was often angry and ashamed that he had no place to die.
translations.idiomatic: Du himself, seeing authority slack and the throne in decline, was often tormented that he had not yet found a place to die for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 自行營歸，知賊曲折，帝益信杖。

translations.literal: On his return from the field headquarters he knew the rebels' twists and turns; the emperor trusted and relied on him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from headquarters he understood the rebels' situation in detail, and the emperor relied on him still more.

sentences.zh: 及病創一再旬，分衛兵護第，存候踵路。

translations.literal: When his wound had troubled him for a dozen or so days, guards were assigned to protect his residence, and callers asking after him filled the road.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly two weeks while he convalesced, imperial guards were posted at his house and well-wishers lined the streets.

sentences.zh: 疾愈，詔毋須宣政衙，即對延英，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When his illness was cured, he was ordered not to need the Xuanzheng Yamen but to answer directly at Yanying, and was appointed vice director of the Central Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Once he recovered, the emperor excused him from the morning audience at Xuanzheng Gate and received him directly in the Yanying Hall, appointing him vice director of the Central Secretariat and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 時方連諸道兵，環挐不解，內外大恐，人累息。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of the various circuits were being joined in succession, encircling and pressing without release; inside and outside there was great fear, and people repeatedly sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Armies from every circuit were being massed in an unrelenting siege; court and country were gripped by fear, and people scarcely dared breathe.

sentences.zh: 及度當國，外內始安。

translations.literal: When Du took charge of the state, outside and inside first became secure.
translations.idiomatic: Once Du took charge of the government, the realm at last grew calm.

sentences.zh: 由是討賊益急。

translations.literal: From this the campaign against the rebels became all the more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign against the rebels was pressed with renewed urgency.

sentences.zh: 始，德宗時尚何伺，中朝士相過，金吾輒飛啟，宰相至闔門謝賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in Dezong's time they still favored He Si; when court gentlemen visited one another the Golden Guards would immediately fly a report, and chief ministers would go to the palace gate to apologize to their guests.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong the court still indulged the informer He Si: whenever officials called on one another the Golden Guards would report it at once, and chief ministers had to apologize at the palace gate for receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 度以時多故，宜延天下髦英咨籌策，乃建請還第與士大夫相見，詔可。

translations.literal: Du, because the times had many troubles, held that the empire's outstanding talents should be invited to consult on plans and strategies, and therefore proposed returning to his residence to meet scholars and officials; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Du argued that in such troubled times the court should summon the empire's best minds for counsel, and petitioned to receive visitors at his residence. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 會莊憲太后崩，為禮儀使。

translations.literal: It happened that Empress Dowager Zhuangxian died; he was made commissioner of rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Zhuangxian died, he was appointed commissioner of funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽政，議置塚宰，度曰：「塚宰，商、週六官首，秉統百僚，王者諒暗，有權聽之制。

translations.literal: The emperor did not attend to government; they discussed appointing a regent chancellor. Du said: "The regent chancellor was head of the six offices in Shang and Zhou, holding and directing the hundred officials; when the king observed mourning seclusion there was the system of provisional hearing of affairs."
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor withdrew from government, the court debated appointing a regent chancellor. Du said, "The regent chancellor was the head of the six ministries in antiquity, directing all officials while the king mourned in seclusion under the provisional-hearing system."

sentences.zh: 曆世官廢，故國朝置否不常，不宜徇空名，稽樞務。

translations.literal: Through the ages the office was abandoned, so in our dynasty whether it is established or not is not constant; one should not follow an empty title and delay pivotal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That office had long fallen into disuse, and our dynasty had appointed it only intermittently. We should not cling to an empty title and stall urgent state business.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔百司權聽中書門下處可。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued that the hundred offices should provisionally hear what the Secretariat and Chancellery might dispose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore ordered all agencies to provisionally accept decisions from the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 王鍔死，家奴告鍔子稷易父奏末，冒遺獻。

translations.literal: When Wang E died, a household slave reported that E's son Ji had altered the end of his father's memorial and falsely presented it as a posthumous submission.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang E died, a household slave accused his son Ji of tampering with the end of his father's final memorial and presenting it as a posthumous petition.

sentences.zh: 帝留奴仗內，遣使者如東都按責其貲。

translations.literal: The emperor kept the slave in the inner palace guard, and sent envoys to the eastern capital to investigate and seize his property.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept the slave in the inner guard and sent envoys to Luoyang to investigate and seize the family's assets.

sentences.zh: 度諫曰：「自鍔死，數有獻。

translations.literal: Du remonstrated, saying: "Since E's death there have been several submissions.
translations.idiomatic: Du remonstrated, "Since Wang E's death there have already been several accusations.

sentences.zh: 今因告訐而檢省其私，臣恐天下將帥聞之，有以家為計者。

translations.literal: Now because of an informer's accusation we inspect and examine his private affairs; I fear that when the empire's military governors hear of this, some will take their households into account."
translations.idiomatic: If we now ransack a general's household on the word of an informer, I fear every commander in the realm will start planning for his family's safety."

sentences.zh: 」帝悟，殺二奴，還使者。

translations.literal: The emperor understood, executed the two slaves, and returned the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his point, executed the two slaves, and recalled the envoys.

sentences.zh: 于時，討蔡數不利，群臣爭請罷兵，錢徽、蕭俛尤確苦。

translations.literal: At that time the campaign against Cai had several times been unfavorable; the ministers all vied to request stopping the army, Qian Hui and Xiao Fu being especially firm and bitter.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign against Cai had met repeated setbacks, and ministers clamored to withdraw the armies, Qian Hui and Xiao Fu being the most insistent.

sentences.zh: 度奏：「病在腹心，不時去，且為大患。

translations.literal: Du memorialized: "The disease is in the heart and belly; if it is not removed in time, it will moreover become a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Du memorialized, "The disease lies in the empire's heartland. If it is not cut out in time it will become a far greater calamity.

sentences.zh: 不然，兩河亦將視此為逆順。

translations.literal: Otherwise the two He regions will also take this as their standard of obedience and rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the two He circuits will judge the throne by whether we yield here."

sentences.zh: 」會唐鄧節度使高霞寓戰卻，它相揣帝厭兵，欲赦賊，鉤上指。

translations.literal: It happened that Tang-Deng military governor Gao Xiayu was defeated in battle; the other chief ministers guessed the emperor was weary of war and wished to pardon the rebels, and hooked their upper fingers [in a secret signal].
translations.idiomatic: When Tang-Deng governor Gao Xiayu suffered a defeat, other chief ministers, guessing that the emperor was weary of war and inclined to pardon the rebels, exchanged knowing glances.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「一勝一負，兵家常勢。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "One victory and one defeat are the army's constant pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Victory and defeat alternate—that is the nature of war.

sentences.zh: 若師常利，則古何憚用兵耶？

translations.literal: If armies were always advantageous, why would the ancients have feared using troops?"
translations.idiomatic: If armies always won, why would the ancients have dreaded war?"

sentences.zh: 雖累聖亦不應留賊付朕。

translations.literal: Even successive sage emperors ought not to have left rebels to hand over to me.
translations.idiomatic: Even my sage forebears would not have left rebels for me to inherit.

sentences.zh: 今但論帥臣勇怯、兵強弱、處置何如耳，渠一敗便沮成計乎？

translations.literal: Now we only discuss whether commanders are brave or timid, troops strong or weak, and dispositions how they are—shall one defeat then frustrate the completed plan?"
translations.idiomatic: We should judge our commanders' courage, our armies' strength, and our strategy—not abandon a settled plan because of one defeat."

sentences.zh: 」於是左右不能容其間。

translations.literal: From this the attendants at left and right could not insert themselves between.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's attendants could no longer intervene.

sentences.zh: 十二年，宰相逢吉、涯建言：「餉億煩匱，宜休師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, chief ministers Feng Ji and Li Ya proposed: "Supplies in the hundreds of millions are troublesome and exhausting; the army should be rested."
translations.idiomatic: In 817 the chief ministers Feng Ji and Li Ya urged, "The cost of supplies runs into the hundreds of millions and is bankrupting the treasury. We should halt the campaign."

sentences.zh: 」唯度請身督戰，帝獨目度留，曰：「果為朕行乎？

translations.literal: Only Du requested to go in person to supervise the campaign. The emperor alone fixed his eyes on Du and kept him, saying: "Will you truly go for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Only Du volunteered to take command in person. The emperor fixed his gaze on Du alone and asked, "Will you truly go for me?"

sentences.zh: 」度俯伏流涕曰：「臣誓不與賊偕存。

translations.literal: Du prostrated himself with flowing tears and said: "Your servant vows not to coexist with the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Du prostrated himself, weeping, and said, "I swear I shall not survive while the rebels do."

sentences.zh: 」即拜門下侍郎、平章事、彰義軍節度、淮西宣慰招討處置使。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed vice director of the Gate Department, Grand Councillor, military commissioner of Zhangyi Army, and pacification, recruitment, and disposition commissioner for Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once appointed vice director of the Gate Department, grand councillor, military commissioner of Zhangyi, and pacification commissioner for the Huai West campaign.

sentences.zh: 度以韓弘領都統，乃上還招討以避弘，然實行都統事。

translations.literal: Because Han Hong held the overall command, Du memorialized to return the recruitment title to avoid Hong, yet in fact carried out the overall commander's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han Hong held the title of overall commander, Du petitioned to surrender the recruitment commission to avoid clashing with him, yet in practice exercised overall command.

sentences.zh: 又制詔有異辭，欲激賊怒弘者，意弘怏怏則度無與共功。

translations.literal: Moreover the drafted edict had unusual wording, intending to provoke the rebels to anger Hong—the idea being that if Hong were displeased, Du would have no one with whom to share merit.
translations.idiomatic: A drafted edict also contained provocative wording meant to inflame the rebels against Han Hong, on the theory that if Hong were offended, Du would fight the war alone.

sentences.zh: 度請易其辭，窒疑間之嫌。

translations.literal: Du requested changing its wording to block suspicion and estrangement between them.
translations.idiomatic: Du asked that the wording be changed to remove any cause for suspicion between them.

sentences.zh: 於是表馬總為宣慰副使，韓愈行軍司馬，李正封、馮宿、李宗閔備兩使幕府。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized Ma Zong as deputy pacification commissioner, Han Yu as campaign staff officer, and Li Zhengfeng, Feng Su, and Li Zongmin to complete the staffs of both commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Ma Zong as deputy pacification commissioner, Han Yu as campaign staff officer, and Li Zhengfeng, Feng Su, and Li Zongmin to staff both headquarters.

sentences.zh: 入對延英，曰：「主憂臣辱，義在必死。

translations.literal: Entering audience at Yanying, he said: "When the ruler worries the minister is shamed; righteousness lies in certain death.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave in the Yanying Hall, he said, "When the ruler is troubled, the minister is shamed. Righteousness demands that I die if need be.

sentences.zh: 賊未授首，臣無還期。

translations.literal: Until the rebels' heads are delivered, your servant has no date of return."
translations.idiomatic: Until the rebel leaders' heads are brought in, I have no date of return."

sentences.zh: 」帝壯之，為流涕。

translations.literal: The emperor was stirred by his spirit and wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and wept.

sentences.zh: 及行，禦通化門臨遣，賜通天禦帶，發神策騎三百為衛。

translations.literal: When he set out, the emperor came to Tonghua Gate to see him off in person, bestowed the Tongtian imperial belt, and dispatched three hundred Shence cavalry as escort.
translations.idiomatic: As he departed, the emperor saw him off in person at Tonghua Gate, granted him the Tongtian imperial belt, and assigned three hundred Shence horsemen as his guard.

sentences.zh: 初，逢吉忌度，帝惡居中撓沮，出之外。

translations.literal: At the beginning Feng Ji was jealous of Du; the emperor disliked obstruction at the center and sent him outside.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ji had long resented Du, and the emperor, weary of obstruction at court, was glad to send him to the front.

sentences.zh: 度屯郾城，勞諸軍，宣朝廷厚意，士奮於勇。

translations.literal: Du encamped at Yancheng, comforted the various armies, proclaimed the court's generous intent, and the soldiers were stirred in courage.
translations.idiomatic: Du encamped at Yancheng, reviewed the troops, and proclaimed the court's goodwill until the soldiers' fighting spirit doubled.

sentences.zh: 是時，諸道兵悉中官統監，自處進退。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of the various circuits were all supervised by eunuch commanders, who decided advance and retreat on their own.
translations.idiomatic: At that time every circuit army was supervised by eunuch overseers who decided advances and retreats on their own.

sentences.zh: 度奏罷之，使將得顓制，號令一，戰氣倍。

translations.literal: Du memorialized to abolish them, so that generals could obtain sole control; orders were unified and fighting spirit doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Du petitioned to abolish the eunuch supervisors so that field commanders could exercise sole authority. Once orders were unified, morale doubled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李愬夜入懸瓠城，縛吳元濟以報。

translations.literal: Before long Li Su entered Xuanchi city by night and bound Wu Yuanji to report.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Su stormed Xuanchi by night and sent word that Wu Yuanji had been captured.

sentences.zh: 度遣馬總先入蔡，明日，統洄曲降卒萬人持節徐進，撫定其人。

translations.literal: Du sent Ma Zong to enter Cai first; the next day he led ten thousand surrendered troops of Huaiqu, holding his staff and advancing slowly, and pacified and settled the people.
translations.idiomatic: Du sent Ma Zong ahead into Cai. The next day he entered at the head of ten thousand surrendered Huaiqu troops, staff in hand, moving slowly to reassure the populace.

sentences.zh: 初，元濟禁偶語於道，夜不然燭，酒食相饋遺者以軍法論。

translations.literal: At first Yuanji had forbidden paired speech on the roads, candles were not lit at night, and those who gave food and drink to one another were judged by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuanji, paired conversation in the streets had been forbidden, lamps were banned at night, and sharing food or drink was punishable by military law.

sentences.zh: 度視事，下令唯盜賊、鬥死抵法，餘一蠲除，往來不限晝夜，民始知有生之樂。

translations.literal: When Du took office he ordered that only thieves and robbers and those who died in brawls would be subject to law; the rest were entirely remitted, and coming and going were not limited to day or night; the people first knew the joy of being alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Du took office he decreed that only theft and brawling deaths would be punished, abolished all other restrictions, and allowed free movement day and night. The people at last tasted what it meant to live.

sentences.zh: 度以蔡牙卒侍帳下，或謂：「反側未安，不可去備。

translations.literal: Du had Cai garrison soldiers attend below his tent; some said: "Those who turn and hesitate are not yet secure; one cannot remove precautions."
translations.idiomatic: Du kept former Cai garrison troops as his personal guard. Some warned, "Loyalty is still uncertain—you must not lower your guard."

sentences.zh: 」度笑曰：「吾為彰義節度，元惡已擒，人皆吾人也！

translations.literal: Du laughed and said: "I am military commissioner of Zhangyi; the chief villain has already been captured—all people are my people!"
translations.idiomatic: Du laughed and said, "I am military commissioner of Zhangyi. The chief villain is captured—every man here is my man!"

sentences.zh: 」眾感泣。

translations.literal: The crowd was moved and wept.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd wept at his words.

sentences.zh: 既而申、光平定，以馬總為留後。

translations.literal: Before long Shen and Guang were pacified, and Ma Zong was made acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shen and Guang were pacified as well, and Ma Zong was left as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 度入朝，會帝以二劍付監軍梁守謙，使悉誅賊將。

translations.literal: Du entered court; it happened that the emperor had given two swords to army supervisor Liang Shouqian, ordering him to execute all the rebel generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Du returned to court, the emperor had just given two swords to army supervisor Liang Shouqian with orders to execute every rebel officer.

sentences.zh: 度遇諸郾城，復與入蔡，商罪議誅。

translations.literal: Du met him at Yancheng, again entered Cai with him, and discussed crimes and deliberated executions.
translations.idiomatic: Du met him at Yancheng, re-entered Cai with him, and debated which men deserved death.

sentences.zh: 守謙請如詔，度固不然，騰奏申解，全宥者甚眾。

translations.literal: Shouqian requested acting according to the edict; Du firmly disagreed, sent up a rapid memorial explaining and pleading, and those wholly pardoned were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian urged following the edict to the letter, but Du refused. He memorialized urgently on the men's behalf, and a great many were spared.

sentences.zh: 策勳進金紫光祿大夫、弘文館大學士、上柱國、晉國公，戶三千，復知政事。

translations.literal: For his merit in planning he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Hanlin academician of the Hongwen Hall, Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of Jin with three thousand households, and again put in charge of government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded for his service, he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Hanlin academician of the Hongwen Hall, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Duke of Jin with three thousand households, and restored to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 程異、皇甫鎛以言財賦幸，俄得宰相。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi and Huangfu Bo gained favor through speaking on finances and taxes, and soon obtained the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi and Huangfu Bo won favor by lecturing on fiscal policy and soon became chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 度三上書極論不可，帝不納。

translations.literal: Du three times sent up memorials vehemently arguing it could not be done; the emperor did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Du memorialized three times in the strongest terms against their appointment, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 自上印，又不聽。

translations.literal: He submitted his seal from above; again it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He offered his seal of office; again the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 纖人始得乘罅。

translations.literal: Petty men thereupon were able to exploit the cracks.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men at court at last found their opening.

sentences.zh: 初，蔡平，王承宗懼，度遣辯士柏耆脅說，乃獻德、棣二州，納質子。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Cai was pacified, Wang Chengzong was afraid; Du sent the debater Bo Qi to coerce and persuade him, and he thereupon presented the two prefectures of De and Di and sent in a hostage son.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai fell, Wang Chengzong was terrified. Du sent the negotiator Bo Qi to pressure him, and Chengzong surrendered the De and Di prefectures and sent his son as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 又諭程權入覲。

translations.literal: He also instructed Cheng Quan to enter court for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Du also persuaded Cheng Quan to come to court in person.

sentences.zh: 始判滄、景、德、棣為一鎮，朝廷命帥，而承宗勢乃離。

translations.literal: For the first time Cang, Jing, De, and Di were combined into one circuit; the court appointed a commander, and Chengzong's power was thereby divided.
translations.idiomatic: The court for the first time combined Cang, Jing, De, and Di into a single circuit under an imperial appointee, splitting Chengzong's power.

sentences.zh: 李師道怙強，度密勸帝誅之。

translations.literal: Li Shidao relied on his strength; Du secretly urged the emperor to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao still relied on his strength, and Du privately urged the emperor to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 乃詔宣武、義成、武寧、橫海四節度會田弘正致討。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued that the four military commissioners of Xuanwu, Yicheng, Wuning, and Henghai should join Tian Hongzheng to launch the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Xuanwu, Yicheng, Wuning, and Henghai commissioners to join Tian Hongzheng in a coordinated attack.

sentences.zh: 弘正請自黎陽濟，合諸節度兵，宰相皆謂宜。

translations.literal: Hongzheng requested to cross from Liyang himself and unite the armies of the various commissioners; the chief ministers all said it was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng proposed crossing at Liyang and combining all the circuit armies. The chief ministers all approved.

sentences.zh: 度曰：「魏博軍度黎陽，即叩賊境，封畛比聯，易生顧望，是自戰其地。

translations.literal: Du said: "If the Weibo army crosses Liyang, it immediately knocks on the rebels' territory; borders adjoin one another and it is easy to give rise to looking back and hesitating—it is fighting on its own ground."
translations.idiomatic: Du objected, "If the Weibo army crosses at Liyang it enters enemy territory immediately, with home districts just behind. The men will look over their shoulders—it would be fighting on their own ground."

sentences.zh: 弘正、光顏素少斷，士心盤桓，果不可用。

translations.literal: Hongzheng and Guangyan by nature lack decisiveness; soldiers' hearts linger and turn—indeed they cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng and Guangyan have never been decisive commanders. Their troops' loyalty wavers. That plan truly will not work."

sentences.zh: 不如養威河北，須霜降水落，絕陽劉，深抵鄆，以營陽穀，則人人殊死，賊勢窮矣。

translations.literal: It would be better to nurture prestige north of the Yellow River, wait until frost falls and waters subside, cut off Yangliu, press deep to Yun, and encamp at Yanggu—then every man will fight to a different death and the rebels' power will be exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Better to build strength north of the river, wait until frost and low water, cut Yangliu, drive deep toward Yun, and camp at Yanggu. Then every soldier will fight as if his life depended on it, and the rebels will be finished."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「善。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 」詔弘正如度言。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hongzheng to act as Du had said.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Hongzheng to follow Du's plan.

sentences.zh: 弘正奉詔，師道果禽。

translations.literal: Hongzheng received the edict, and Shidao was indeed captured.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng obeyed, and Shidao was duly captured.

sentences.zh: 大賈張陟負五坊息錢，上命坊使楊朝汶收其家簿，閱貸錢雖已償，悉鉤止，根引數十百人，列箠挺脅不承。

translations.literal: The great merchant Zhang Zhi owed interest money to the Five Wards; the emperor ordered Ward envoy Yang Chaowen to seize his household registers. Examining loans, though they had already been repaid, all were hooked and stopped; tracing back, several tens and hundreds of people were implicated, lined up with cudgels and staffs to coerce non-confession.
translations.idiomatic: The great merchant Zhang Zhi owed interest to the Five Wards. The emperor ordered ward envoy Yang Chaowen to seize his account books. Even loans already repaid were seized, and the investigation dragged in hundreds of people who were lined up and beaten until they confessed.

sentences.zh: 又獲盧大夫逋券，捕盧坦家客責償，久乃悟盧群券。

translations.literal: He also obtained fleeing-debt notes of Grandee Lu, arrested Lu Tan's household guest to demand repayment, and only after a long while realized they were Lu Qun's notes.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized promissory notes belonging to the fugitive Lu, arrested a retainer of Lu Tan's household to collect repayment, and only much later discovered they were Lu Qun's notes.

sentences.zh: 坦子上訴，朝汶讕語：「錢入禁中，何可得？

translations.literal: Tan's son appealed upward; Chaowen spoke evasively: "The money entered the forbidden precinct—how can it be obtained?"
translations.idiomatic: Tan appealed on his son's behalf. Chaowen answered evasively, "The money went into the inner palace. How can it be recovered?"

sentences.zh: 」御史中丞蕭俛及諫官列陳中人橫恣，度亦極言之。

translations.literal: Vice censor-in-chief Xiao Fu and remonstrating officials in succession presented that the inner eunuchs were overbearing and willful; Du also spoke to the utmost on it.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Xiao Fu and the remonstrance officials lined up to denounce the eunuchs' arrogance, and Du spoke with equal force.

sentences.zh: 時方討鄆，帝曰：「姑議東軍，此細事，我自處辦。

translations.literal: At that time they were campaigning against Yun; the emperor said: "For now discuss the eastern armies—this is a minor matter; I myself will handle it."
translations.idiomatic: The court was then campaigning against Yun. The emperor said, "Let us discuss the eastern armies for now. This petty matter I will handle myself."

sentences.zh: 」度曰：「兵事不理，止山東；

translations.literal: Du said: "If military affairs are not managed, it stops at Shandong alone;"
translations.idiomatic: Du replied, "Neglect military affairs and the trouble stops at Shandong alone;

sentences.zh: 中人橫暴，將亂都下。

translations.literal: if inner eunuchs are overbearing and violent, they will throw the capital into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: let eunuchs run riot in the capital and the realm itself will be thrown into chaos."

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅，徐乃悟，讓朝汶曰：「以爾，使我羞見宰相！

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, but slowly understood, and rebuked Chaowen: "Because of you I am ashamed to face the chief ministers!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased, but gradually understood. He rebuked Chaowen: "Because of you I am ashamed to face my chief ministers!"

sentences.zh: 」命殺之，而原系者。

translations.literal: He ordered him killed and pardoned those imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Chaowen executed and released those who had been imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 繇是京師澄肅。

translations.literal: From this the capital grew clear and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the capital grew calm and orderly.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗語：「臣事君，當勵善底公，朕惡夫樹黨者。

translations.literal: The emperor once said: "Ministers serving the ruler should encourage good and support public fairness; I hate those who form factions."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once remarked, "A minister should encourage goodness and uphold the public good. I despise men who form factions."

sentences.zh: 」度曰：「君子小人以類而聚，未有無徒者。

translations.literal: Du said: "Gentlemen and petty men gather by kind—there never was one without followers."
translations.idiomatic: Du said, "Gentlemen and petty men alike gather their kind. No man stands entirely alone."

sentences.zh: 君子之徒同德，小人之徒同惡，外甚類，中實遠，在陛下觀所行則辨。

translations.literal: Gentlemen's followers share virtue, petty men's share wickedness; outwardly very alike, inwardly truly far—let Your Majesty observe what they do and you will distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: The followers of gentlemen share their virtue; the followers of petty men share their wickedness. Outwardly they look alike, inwardly they are worlds apart. Your Majesty has only to watch what men do."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「言者大抵若此，朕豈易辨之？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Speakers are mostly like this—how can I easily distinguish?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Most courtiers speak this way. How can I easily tell them apart?"

sentences.zh: 」度退，喜曰：「上以為難辨則易，以為易辨則難，君子小人行判矣。

translations.literal: Du withdrew, pleased, saying: "If the ruler thinks it hard to distinguish, it is easy; if he thinks it easy, it is hard—the conduct of gentleman and petty man is decided."
translations.idiomatic: Du withdrew, pleased. "When the ruler thinks distinction is hard, it is easy; when he thinks it is easy, it is hard. The line between gentleman and petty man is already drawn."

sentences.zh: 」已而卒為異、鎛所構，以檢校尚書右僕射兼門下侍郎平章事為河東節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was at last framed by Yi and Bo, and made military commissioner of Hedong with the titular posts of acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councillor through the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was framed by Cheng Yi and Huangfu Bo and sent out as military commissioner of Hedong, though still bearing the titular rank of chief minister.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，進檢校司空。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, Du was advanced to acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong succeeded, Du was promoted to acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 硃克融、王廷湊亂河朔，加度鎮州行營招討使。

translations.literal: Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou threw Hebei into disorder; Du was additionally made recruitment commissioner of the Zhenzhou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou rebelled in Hebei, Du was appointed recruitment commissioner at the Zhenzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時帝以李光顏、烏重胤爪牙將，倚以擊賊，兵十余萬，有所畏，無尺寸功。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor regarded Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin as claw-and-fang generals, relied on them to strike the rebels, had an army of more than a hundred thousand, yet they had something they feared and achieved not a fraction of an inch of merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had relied on Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin, his fiercest generals, with more than a hundred thousand men to crush the rebels, yet they fought cautiously and won not a single victory.

sentences.zh: 度既受命，入賊境，數斬將以聞。

translations.literal: Once Du received the mandate, he entered rebel territory and repeatedly beheaded generals to report.
translations.idiomatic: Once Du took command, he crossed into rebel territory and repeatedly reported the beheading of enemy generals.

sentences.zh: 俄兼押北山諸蕃使。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made commissioner over the various tribes north of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made commissioner over the northern frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 時元稹顯結宦官魏弘簡求執政，憚度復當國，因經制軍事，數居中持梗，不使有功。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zhen openly allied with the eunuch Wei Hongjian to seek power, feared Du's return to head the state, and therefore managed military affairs, repeatedly obstructing at the center and not allowing achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen had openly allied with the eunuch Wei Hongjian to seize power. Fearing Du's return to office, he used his control of military affairs to block Du repeatedly and deny him any success.

sentences.zh: 度恐亂作，即上書痛暴稹過惡。

translations.literal: Du feared disorder would arise and immediately sent up a memorial bitterly exposing Zhen's faults and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing disorder, Du memorialized at once, denouncing Yuan Zhen's crimes in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，罷弘簡、稹近職。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice and removed Hongjian and Zhen from close offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice but to remove Hongjian and Zhen from their posts at court.

sentences.zh: 俄擢稹宰相，以度守司空、平章事、東都留守。

translations.literal: Before long Zhen was elevated to chief minister, and Du was made acting Minister of Works, grand councillor, and eastern capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuan Zhen was made chief minister anyway, while Du was left as acting Minister of Works, grand councillor in name only, and regent of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 諫官叩延英，言不可罷度兵，搖眾心。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials knocked at Yanying, saying one could not remove Du from the army—it would shake popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials pleaded at the Yanying Hall that stripping Du of military command would shake the army's morale.

sentences.zh: 帝不召。

translations.literal: The emperor did not summon them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not receive them.

sentences.zh: 於是交章極論，未之省。

translations.literal: Thereupon they sent up memorials in succession arguing to the utmost, but he did not reflect on it.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials poured in making the same argument, but the emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 會中人使幽、鎮還，言：「軍中謂度在朝，而兩河諸侯忠者懷，強者畏。

translations.literal: It happened that an inner eunuch envoy returned from You and Zhen and said: "In the army they say that while Du is at court, the various lords of the two He regions—those loyal are reassured, those strong are in awe."
translations.idiomatic: An eunuch envoy returned from You and Zhen reporting, "The armies say that while Du remains at court, loyal lords in the two He regions take heart and strong ones stand in awe."

sentences.zh: 今居東，人人失望。

translations.literal: Now that he dwells in the east, every man is disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has been sent east, everyone is disappointed."

sentences.zh: 」帝悟，詔度由太原朝京師。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and ordered Du to come from Taiyuan to court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and ordered Du to come from Taiyuan to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及陛見，始陳二賊畔換，受命無功，並陳所以入覲意，感概流涕。

translations.literal: When he had audience at the steps, he first presented that the two rebels had turned disloyal, that he had received the mandate without achievement, and also presented the reason for his coming to audience; moved, he shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he explained that the two rebels had turned traitor, that he had accepted command without winning success, and why he had come to court in person. He wept with emotion.

sentences.zh: 伏未起，謁者欲宣旨，帝遽曰：「朕當延英待卿！

translations.literal: He had not yet risen from prostration when the usher wished to proclaim the edict; the emperor hastily said: "I shall await you at Yanying!"
translations.idiomatic: Before he could rise, the usher moved to announce an edict. The emperor said hastily, "I shall await you in the Yanying Hall!"

sentences.zh: 」始，議者謂度無奧援，且久外，為奸憸拫抑，慮帝未能明其忠。

translations.literal: At the beginning counsellors said Du had no deep backing, and having long been outside, was suppressed by treacherous villains; they feared the emperor could not make clear his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: At first observers said Du lacked powerful patrons, had been long abroad, and had been crushed by schemers; they feared the emperor would not see his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及進見，辭切氣怡，卓然當天子意。

translations.literal: When he entered audience his words were cutting and his bearing easy; outstandingly he matched the Son of Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When he appeared, his words were forceful and his manner composed. He struck the emperor exactly as he wished.

sentences.zh: 在位聞者皆竦，毅將貴臣至齎咨出涕。

translations.literal: Those in office who heard were all startled; stalwart generals and noble ministers even brought inquiries and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Those present were startled. Even hardened generals and high nobles came to inquire and left in tears.

sentences.zh: 舊儀，閣中群臣未退，宰相不奏事，稱賀則謁者答。

translations.literal: By old ritual, while the ministers in the pavilion had not withdrawn, the chief minister did not present business; if congratulations were offered the usher answered.
translations.idiomatic: By old ritual, while ministers had not yet withdrawn from the pavilion, the chief minister did not present business, and congratulations were answered by the usher alone.

sentences.zh: 帝以度勳德，故待以殊禮。

translations.literal: Because of Du's merit and virtue the emperor therefore treated him with special ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Du's merit and stature, the emperor treated him with exceptional ceremony.

sentences.zh: 度之行，移克融、廷湊書，開說諄遝，傅以大誼，二人不敢桀，皆願罷兵。

translations.literal: On Du's journey he sent letters to Kerong and Tingcou, expounded earnestly and repeatedly, and imbued them with great principle; the two men did not dare be obstinate and both wished to cease arms.
translations.idiomatic: On his journey Du wrote to Kerong and Tingcou, reasoning with them at length on the larger principles of loyalty. Neither dared defy him, and both offered to lay down arms.

sentences.zh: 帝方憂深州圍，欲必出牛元翼，更使度騰書布旨。

translations.literal: The emperor was then worried about the siege of Shenzhou and wished by all means to extricate Niu Yuanji; he again had Du send up rapid letters to proclaim the intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was anxious about the siege of Shenzhou and determined to rescue Niu Yuanji. He again had Du send urgent letters proclaiming the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「賊知度失兵柄，必背約顧望。

translations.literal: Some said: "The rebels, knowing Du has lost military authority, will surely break the agreement and look back hesitating."
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "Once the rebels learn Du has lost military authority, they will surely break their promises and hesitate."

sentences.zh: 」帝釋然，乃拜度守司徒，領淮南節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor was relieved and thereupon appointed Du acting Minister of Education and military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was reassured and appointed Du Minister of Education and military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 會昭義監軍劉承偕慢劉悟，舉軍嘩怒，執承偕，悟拘以聞。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhaoyi army supervisor Liu Chengxie slighted Liu Wu; the whole army clamored in anger, seized Chengxie, and Wu detained him to report.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhaoyi army supervisor Liu Chengxie insulted Liu Wu. The whole army rose in uproar, seized Chengxie, and Wu reported the matter under restraint.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，問度：「何施而可？

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and asked Du: "What measure will do?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and asked Du, "What can be done?"

sentences.zh: 」度頓首謝：「籓臣不與政。

translations.literal: Du knocked his head and declined: "A frontier minister does not participate in government."
translations.idiomatic: Du kowtowed and declined. "A frontier minister does not meddle in central government."

sentences.zh: 」辭不對。

translations.literal: He declined and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 帝強之，度曰：「臣素知承偕怙寵，悟不能堪，嘗以書訴臣。

translations.literal: The emperor pressed him; Du said: "Your servant has long known Chengxie relied on favor, and Wu could not bear it—he once complained to your servant in a letter."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed him. Du said, "I have long known Chengxie abused imperial favor and that Wu could not endure it. Wu once wrote to me to complain."

sentences.zh: 是時，中人趙弘亮在行營知狀，欲持悟書以奏，陛下亦知之邪？

translations.literal: At that time the inner eunuch Zhao Hongliang at the field headquarters knew the situation and wished to take Wu's letter to memorialize—does Your Majesty also know of this?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eunuch Zhao Hongliang at headquarters knew the facts and meant to present Wu's letter. Did Your Majesty know of this?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我不及知。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I did not reach knowing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I did not know."

sentences.zh: 顧悟誠惡之，胡不自聞，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet if Wu truly hated him, why did he not himself report—how so?"
translations.idiomatic: If Wu truly hated him, why did he not report it himself?"

sentences.zh: 」度曰：「雖悟得聞，恐陛下不必聽。

translations.literal: Du said: "Though Wu could have it heard, I fear Your Majesty would not necessarily listen."
translations.idiomatic: Du said, "Even if Wu had reported it, I fear Your Majesty might not have listened."

sentences.zh: 且臣視天顏不咫尺，比尚未能決，千里單言，可悟聖聽哉？

translations.literal: Moreover your servant views the heavenly countenance not a foot away—just now he still could not decide; a thousand li away with a single word, could Wu reach the sage ear?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I stand before Your Majesty face to face and still cannot always win a decision. How could a lone report from a thousand li away reach your ears?"

sentences.zh: 」帝亟曰：「前語姑置，直謂今日奈何？

translations.literal: The emperor urgently said: "Set aside the earlier words for now—speak directly: what of today?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said urgently, "Leave that aside. Tell me plainly what to do today."

sentences.zh: 」度曰：「必欲收忠義心，使帥臣死節，獨斬承偕，則四方群盜隱然破膽矣。

translations.literal: Du said: "If you must win loyal and righteous hearts and make commanders die for principle, execute Chengxie alone, and the bandits everywhere will inwardly have their courage broken."
translations.idiomatic: Du said, "If you wish to win loyal hearts and make commanders die for their duty, execute Chengxie alone. Rebels everywhere will lose their nerve at once."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「顧太后養為子，且我何愛？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Considering the empress dowager raised him as a son, what love do I have for him?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The empress dowager raised him as her son. What do I owe him?"

sentences.zh: 更言其次。

translations.literal: Speak of the next option.
translations.idiomatic: Tell me the next option.

sentences.zh: 」度曰：「投諸荒裔可乎？

translations.literal: Du said: "Cast him to the wild borderlands—would that do?"
translations.idiomatic: Du said, "Could he be exiled to the frontier?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「可。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It will do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」悟果出承偕，昭義遂安。

translations.literal: Wu indeed released Chengxie, and Zhaoyi was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wu released Chengxie, and Zhaoyi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 是時，徐州王智興逐崔群，諸軍盤互河北，進退未一。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Zhixing of Xuzhou drove out Cui Qun; the various armies intertwined across Hebei, and advance and retreat were not unified.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhixing of Xuzhou had driven out Cui Qun, armies were tangled across Hebei, and the campaign lacked a single direction.

sentences.zh: 議者交口請相度，乃以本官兼中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: Counsellors with one voice requested Du as chief minister; he was therefore made in his existing office also Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers unanimously called for Du as chief minister, and he was appointed vice director of the Central Secretariat and grand councillor in addition to his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 權佞側目，謂李逢吉險賊善謀，可以構度，共諷帝自襄陽召逢吉還，拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Powerful sycophants looked askance; they said Li Fengji was a dangerous villain skilled in plotting and could frame Du; together they hinted to the emperor to recall Fengji from Xiangyang and appoint him Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Power-hungry sycophants whispered that Li Fengji was a cunning schemer who could destroy Du. Together they urged the emperor to recall Fengji from Xiangyang and make him Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 度居位再閱月，果為逢吉所間，罷為左僕射。

translations.literal: Du had been in office for two months when he was indeed estranged by Fengji and removed to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Du had been in office barely two months when Fengji estranged him from the emperor and had him demoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝暴風眩，中外不聞問者凡三日。

translations.literal: The emperor was suddenly stricken with wind dizziness; inside and outside heard nothing of him for three days in all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was suddenly stricken with vertigo, and for three days court and country heard nothing from him.

sentences.zh: 度數請到內殿，求立太子，翼日乃見帝，遂立景王為嗣。

translations.literal: Du several times requested entry to the inner hall to ask that a crown prince be established; the next day he was able to see the emperor, and the Jing Prince was thereupon made heir.
translations.idiomatic: Du repeatedly begged admission to the inner palace to urge the naming of an heir. The next day he saw the emperor, and the Jing Prince was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 逢吉既代相，思有以牙孽之，引所厚李仲言、張又新、李續、張權輿等，內結宦官，種支黨，醜沮日聞，乃出度山南西道節度使，奪平章事。

translations.literal: Once Fengji had replaced him as chief minister, he thought to have something to gnaw and harm him; he drew in those he favored—Li Zhongyan, Zhang Youxin, Li Xu, Zhang Quanyu, and others—joined with eunuchs within, planted branch factions, and ugly slanders were heard daily; he then sent Du out as military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit and stripped him of grand councillor rank.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fengji replaced him as chief minister, he sought to destroy him. He gathered his protégés Li Zhongyan, Zhang Youxin, Li Xu, and Zhang Quanyu, allied with eunuchs, planted factions, and spread slanders daily until Du was sent out as commissioner of Shannan West and stripped of the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年，王廷湊屠元翼之家，敬宗嗟惋，歎宰輔非其人，使凶賊熾肆。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changqing, Wang Tingcou slaughtered Yuanji's household; Jingzong sighed in regret and lamented that the chief ministers were not the right men, allowing fierce rebels to blaze unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: In 824 Wang Tingcou massacred Niu Yuanji's household. Emperor Jingzong sighed in grief and lamented that his chief ministers were unworthy men who had let vicious rebels run wild.

sentences.zh: 學士韋處厚上疏曰：「臣聞汲黯在朝，淮南寢謀；

translations.literal: Academician Wei Chuhou sent up a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that with Ji An at court, Huainan laid its plots to rest;
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Wei Chuhou memorialized, "I have heard that while Ji An held court office, Huainan abandoned its plots;

sentences.zh: 幹木處魏，諸侯息兵。

translations.literal: with Gan Mu in Wei, the feudal lords ceased arms."
translations.idiomatic: and while Gan Mu served in Wei, the feudal lords laid down their arms."

sentences.zh: 王霸之理，以一士止百萬之師，一賢制千里之難。

translations.literal: The principle of true kingship and hegemony is that one scholar stops an army of a million, one worthy controls difficulty for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of true kingship is that one worthy man can halt an army of a million and master trouble across a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 裴度元勳巨德，文武兼備，若位岩廟，委參決，必使戎虜畏威，幽、鎮自臣。

translations.literal: Pei Du has original merit and great virtue, combining civil and military; if placed in the lofty temple and entrusted with deliberation and decision, he will surely make barbarian enemies fear his awesomeness, and You and Zhen will submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du is a founding minister of great virtue, skilled in both civil and military affairs. If he were placed at the summit of government and entrusted with decisions, barbarians would fear our might and You and Zhen would submit of themselves.

sentences.zh: 管仲曰：'人離而聽之則愚，合而聽之則聖。

translations.literal: Guan Zhong said: 'If men are apart and one listens, one is foolish; if one listens together, one is sage.'
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong said, 'Listen to men separately and you will be foolish; listen to them together and you will be wise.'

sentences.zh: '治亂之本，非有他術。

translations.literal: The root of order and disorder has no other art."
translations.idiomatic: The root of order and disorder lies in nothing else."

sentences.zh: 陛下當饋而歎，恨無蕭、曹，今一裴度擯棄於外，所以馮唐知漢文帝有頗、牧不能用也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty at meals sighs, regretting there are no Xiao He or Cao Shen; now a single Pei Du is cast aside outside—this is why Feng Tang knew that Emperor Wen of Han had Li Guang and Wei Qing yet could not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sighs at table, lamenting the lack of men like Xiao He and Cao Shen. Yet Pei Du alone has been cast aside. This is why Feng Tang knew that Emperor Wen of Han possessed generals like Li Guang and Wei Qing yet could not use them.

sentences.zh: 」帝感悟，謂處厚曰：「度累為宰相，而官無平章事，謂何？

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to understanding and said to Chuhou: "Du has repeatedly been chief minister, yet his office lacks grand councillor—what does this mean?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and asked Chuhou, "Du has served repeatedly as chief minister, yet his title lacks grand councillor. What does that mean?"

sentences.zh: 」處厚具道其由，帝於是復度兼平章事。

translations.literal: Chuhou fully explained the reason; the emperor thereupon restored Du to concurrent grand councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou explained the whole story, and the emperor restored Du as grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 帝雖孺蒙，然注意度，中人至度所，必丁甯尉安，且示召期。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was young and unlearned, he nevertheless paid attention to Du; when inner eunuchs came to Du's place they were sure to comfort and reassure him and also show the date of summons.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor was young and inexperienced, he kept his eye on Du. Whenever eunuchs visited Du's residence they reassured him and hinted when he would be recalled.

sentences.zh: 寶曆二年，度請入朝，逢吉黨大懼，權輿作偽謠云：「非衣小兒坦其腹，天上有口被驅逐。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoli, Du requested to enter court; Fengji's faction was greatly afraid; Quanyu fabricated a false rhyme saying: "Not-clothes, small child, belly exposed; heaven above has a mouth and is driven away."
translations.idiomatic: In 826 Du petitioned to return to court. Fengji's faction was terrified. Zhang Quanyu forged a prophecy: "The child in plain clothes bares his belly; the mouth in heaven is driven away."

sentences.zh: 」以度平元濟也。

translations.literal: This referred to Du's pacification of Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: It alluded to Du's pacification of Wu Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 都城東西岡六，民間以為乾數，而度第平樂裏，直第五岡。

translations.literal: East and west of the capital were six ridges, which the people took as the qian number; Du's residence was in Pingle Ward, directly on the fifth ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Six ridges lay east and west of the capital, which folk associated with the qian hexagram. Du's house in Pingle Ward stood directly on the fifth ridge.

sentences.zh: 權輿乃言：「度名應圖讖，第據岡原，不召而來，其意可見。

translations.literal: Quanyu then said: "Du's name answers chart prophecies; his residence occupies the ridge plain; without summons he comes—his intent can be seen."
translations.idiomatic: Quanyu then said, "Du's name fulfills a prophecy. His house occupies the sacred ridge. He comes without being summoned. His intent is obvious."

sentences.zh: 」欲以傾度。

translations.literal: He wished thereby to topple Du.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to destroy Du with this.

sentences.zh: 天子獨能明其誣，詔復使輔政。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven alone could make clear the slander and ordered him again to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor alone saw through the slander and ordered Du restored to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝將幸東都，大臣切諫，不納。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor was about to visit the eastern capital; chief ministers remonstrated urgently and he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had planned to visit the eastern capital. Chief ministers remonstrated urgently, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 帝恚曰：「朕意決矣！

translations.literal: The emperor said in anger: "My intent is decided!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "My mind is made up!

sentences.zh: 雖從官宮人自挾糗，無擾百姓。

translations.literal: though attendants and palace women carry their own dry provisions, we will not disturb the common people."
translations.idiomatic: My attendants and palace women will carry their own provisions. The people will not be troubled."

sentences.zh: 」趣有司檢料行宮，中外莫敢言。

translations.literal: He urged the relevant offices to inspect and prepare the traveling palace; inside and outside none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered officials to prepare the traveling palace. No one inside or outside the court dared object.

sentences.zh: 度從容奏：「國家建別都，本備巡幸。

translations.literal: Du calmly presented: "The state established a secondary capital originally to prepare for imperial tours.
translations.idiomatic: Du said calmly, "The state established a secondary capital originally for imperial tours.

sentences.zh: 自艱難以來，宮闕、署屯、百司之區，荒圮弗治，假歲月完新，然後可行。

translations.literal: Since the times of hardship, palace halls, office encampments, and the districts of the hundred offices have lain waste and ruined without repair; borrow months to complete them anew, and only then may you go."
translations.idiomatic: Since the rebellions, the palaces, offices, and government quarters have fallen into ruin. Allow months to restore them, and only then can Your Majesty travel."

sentences.zh: 倉卒無備，有司且得罪。

translations.literal: If you rush without preparation, the relevant offices will at once be guilty.
translations.idiomatic: A hasty departure would leave officials guilty of negligence."

sentences.zh: 」帝悅曰：「群臣諫朕不及此。

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "The ministers remonstrating with me did not reach this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure, "My ministers never advised me this well."

sentences.zh: 如卿言，誠有未便，安用往邪？

translations.literal: As you say, there truly is inconvenience—why need we go?"
translations.idiomatic: As you say, the journey truly would be inconvenient. Why go at all?"

sentences.zh: 」因止行。

translations.literal: He therefore stopped the journey.
translations.idiomatic: He canceled the journey.

sentences.zh: 汴宋觀察使令狐楚言亳州聖水出，飲者疾輒愈。

translations.literal: Bian-Song observation commissioner Linghu Chu reported that sacred water had appeared in Bozhou and those who drank it were immediately cured of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Bian-Song governor Linghu Chu reported that sacred water had appeared in Bozhou and that the sick were cured at once by drinking it.

sentences.zh: 度判曰：「妖由人興，水不自作。

translations.literal: Du judged: "Omens arise from men; water does not act of itself."
translations.idiomatic: Du ruled, "Omens arise from men; water does not act of itself."

sentences.zh: 」命在所禁塞。

translations.literal: He ordered the locality to forbid and block it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the site closed.

sentences.zh: 硃克融執賜衣使者楊文端，詭言慢己，並訴所賜濫惡，又丐假度支帛三十萬匹，不者，軍必有變；

translations.literal: Zhu Kerong seized imperial-gift-robes envoy Yang Wenduan, falsely claiming he had slighted him, and also complained that what was bestowed was excessive and vile; he further begged to borrow three hundred thousand bolts of cloth from the treasury, otherwise the army would surely mutiny;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong seized the imperial gift-robes envoy Yang Wenduan, falsely claiming insult, and complained that the gifts were shoddy. He also demanded three hundred thousand bolts of cloth from the treasury, threatening mutiny otherwise;

sentences.zh: 且請遣工五千助治東都，須天子東巡。

translations.literal: and requested five thousand workmen be sent to help repair the eastern capital, requiring the Son of Heaven's eastern tour.
translations.idiomatic: and asked for five thousand laborers to repair the eastern capital, insisting the emperor must tour east.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，患之，欲遣重臣臨慰。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and troubled by it, and wished to send a weighty minister to go and comfort him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and troubled, and considered sending a senior minister to appease him.

sentences.zh: 度曰：「克融無恚而悖，是將亡。

translations.literal: Du said: "Kerong has no grievance yet is rebellious—he is about to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Du said, "Kerong rebels without real grievance. He is near his end.

sentences.zh: 譬猛虎自哮躍山林，憑窟穴則然，勢不得離其處，人亦不為懼。

translations.literal: It is like a fierce tiger roaring and leaping in mountain forests by itself—relying on its den it is so; its force cannot leave its place, and men are not afraid."
translations.idiomatic: He is like a tiger roaring in the mountains from its den. So long as it cannot leave its lair, men need not fear it."

sentences.zh: 陛下無庸遣重使，第以詔書言：'中人倨驕，須還，我自責譴。

translations.literal: Your Majesty need not send a weighty envoy; only with an edict say: 'The inner attendant was arrogant and proud and must return; I myself will reprove and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty need not send a senior envoy. Simply issue an edict saying, 'The eunuch envoy was arrogant and must return. I shall punish him myself.

sentences.zh: 春服不謹，方詰有司。

translations.literal: Spring garments were not careful—I am just now questioning the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: I was careless about the spring gifts and am already questioning the responsible officials.

sentences.zh: 所上工宜即遣，已詔在所供擬。

translations.literal: The workmen you presented should be sent at once; I have already ordered the locality to supply and prepare them.
translations.idiomatic: The laborers you requested will be sent at once. I have ordered the local authorities to provide them.

sentences.zh: '此則賊謀窮矣。

translations.literal: 'Then the rebels' schemes will be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: 'Then the rebel's schemes will be exhausted.

sentences.zh: 陛下若未能然，則答：'宮室營繕既有序，毋遣工為重勞。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty cannot do so, then reply: 'Palace construction and repair already have their order—do not send workmen for heavy labor.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty cannot do that, reply instead: 'Palace repairs are already in hand. Do not send laborers and burden us further.

sentences.zh: 朝廷緣召發，乃有賜與，朕無所愛，獨與范陽，體不可爾。

translations.literal: The court because of summons and deployment then has bestowals; I have nothing I cherish alone for Fanyang—the principle cannot be so.'
translations.idiomatic: The court grants gifts when armies are mobilized. I favor no region alone, and Fanyang cannot be treated as an exception.'

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 」用度次策。

translations.literal: Du's second plan was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Du's second plan was adopted.

sentences.zh: 克融聽命，歸文端。

translations.literal: Kerong obeyed the order and returned Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: Kerong obeyed and released Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，軍亂，殺克融。

translations.literal: Before long the army mutinied and killed Kerong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the army mutinied and killed him.

sentences.zh: 帝縱弛，日晏坐朝。

translations.literal: The emperor was lax; he sat at court when the day was late.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew lax and held court late in the day.

sentences.zh: 度諫曰：「此陛下月率六七臨朝，天下人知勤政，河朔賊臣皆聳畏。

translations.literal: Du remonstrated: "Formerly Your Majesty attended court six or seven times a month; people throughout the realm knew your diligent government, and rebel ministers north of the Yellow River were all startled in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Du remonstrated, "Your Majesty used to hold court six or seven times a month. The realm knew you were diligent, and rebels in Hebei stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 近開延英益稀，恐萬機奏稟，有所壅閼。

translations.literal: Recently opening Yanying has grown rarer; I fear the myriad affairs presented and reported may be somewhat blocked and obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Recently audiences at Yanying have grown rare. I fear that state business is being blocked.

sentences.zh: 夫頤養之道，常順適時候，則六氣平和，萬壽可保。

translations.literal: The way of nourishing life constantly follows and suits the seasons; then the six qi are peaceful and balanced, and ten thousand years of life can be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The way to preserve health is to follow the seasons. Then the body's energies stay balanced and long life is assured.

sentences.zh: 道家法：'春夏蚤起，取雞鳴時，秋冬晏起，取日出時。

translations.literal: Taoist teaching says: 'In spring and summer rise early, taking the cock-crow hour; in autumn and winter rise late, taking the sun-rise hour.'
translations.idiomatic: Taoist teaching says, 'Rise early in spring and summer at cockcrow, and rise late in autumn and winter at sunrise.'

sentences.zh: 蓋在陽，勝之以陰；

translations.literal: When in yang, overcome it with yin;
translations.idiomatic: When yang prevails, balance it with yin;

sentences.zh: 在陰，勝之以陽。

translations.literal: when in yin, overcome it with yang.
translations.idiomatic: when yin prevails, balance it with yang.

sentences.zh: 今方居盛夏，謂宜詰旦數坐，廣加延問；

translations.literal: Now we are just in deep summer; I hold that you should sit at dawn several times and broadly extend inquiries;
translations.idiomatic: We are now in deep summer. Your Majesty should hold court at dawn and hear reports at length;

sentences.zh: 漏及巳午，則炎赫可畏，聖躬勞矣。

translations.literal: if the clepsydra reaches si and wu, then blazing heat is to be feared and the sacred person is wearied."
translations.idiomatic: but by the si and wu hours the heat is fearsome and Your Majesty will be exhausted."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納，為數視朝。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it, and for a time attended court frequently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and for a time held court more often.

sentences.zh: 未幾，判度支。

translations.literal: Before long he was put in charge of the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was put in charge of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，定策誅劉克明等，迎立江王，是為文宗。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, he settled the policy to execute Liu Keming and others, welcomed and established the Prince of Jiang, who became Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Du helped decide policy, executed Liu Keming and his faction, and enthroned the Prince of Jiang as Emperor Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 加門下侍郎。

translations.literal: He was made vice director of the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 李全略死，子同捷求襲滄景軍。

translations.literal: When Li Quanlue died, his son Tongjie sought to inherit the Cang-Jing army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Quanlue died, his son Tongjie sought to inherit command of the Cang-Jing army.

sentences.zh: 度奏討平之，即陳：「調兵食非宰相事，請罷度支歸有司。

translations.literal: Du memorialized to campaign and pacify them, and at once stated: "Adjusting troops and provisions is not a chief minister's affair—please abolish treasury control and return it to the relevant offices."
translations.idiomatic: Du memorialized to suppress the rebellion, then said, "Managing troops and provisions is not a chief minister's duty. Please return treasury affairs to the proper offices."

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 進階開府儀同三司，賜實封戶三百。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Grand Master with the same ceremonial as the Three Excellencies and granted three hundred households of substantive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies and granted three hundred households of substantive enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 度懇讓不得可，乃受實封。

translations.literal: Du earnestly declined and could not obtain approval; he thereupon accepted the substantive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Du declined earnestly but could not refuse, and accepted the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，數引疾不任機重，願上政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he repeatedly cited illness as unable to bear weighty affairs and wished to submit government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 830 he repeatedly cited illness and asked to resign the heavy duties of government.

sentences.zh: 帝擇上醫護治，中人日勞問相躡，乃詔進司徒、平章軍國重事，須疾已，三日若五日一至中書。

translations.literal: The emperor chose superior physicians to treat him; inner attendants daily came in succession to inquire after him; an edict then advanced him to Minister of Education and Grand Councillor of Important Military and State Affairs—when illness ended, once every three or five days he should come to the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent his best physicians. Eunuchs visited daily. He was promoted to Minister of Education and grand councillor for military and state affairs, with orders to attend the Secretariat every three or five days once he recovered.

sentences.zh: 度讓免冊禮。

translations.literal: Du declined exemption from investiture rites.
translations.idiomatic: Du declined the investiture ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 度自見功高位極，不能無慮，稍詭跡避禍。

translations.literal: Du himself saw merit high and position at the extreme and could not be without anxiety; he slightly disguised his tracks to avoid calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his merit and rank at their peak, Du could not help worrying and began discreetly to lower his profile to avoid disaster.

sentences.zh: 於是牛僧孺、李宗閔同輔政，媢度勳業久居上，欲有所逞，乃共訾其跡損短之，因度辭位，即白帝進兼侍中，出為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Niu Sengru and Li Zongmin jointly assisted government, jealous that Du's merit and achievement had long stood above them and wishing to display themselves; they together criticized his conduct and diminished him, and because Du resigned office they immediately informed the emperor to advance him concurrently as Palace Attendant and send him out as military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru and Li Zongmin, now sharing power, envied Du's long supremacy and sought to bring him down. They slandered him until he resigned, then had him promoted in title to Palace Attendant but sent out as commissioner of Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 白罷元和所置臨漢監，數千馬納之校，以善田四百頃還襄人。

translations.literal: He reported abolishing the Linhan supervisor established in Yuanhe, turned several thousand horses over to the stud farms, and returned four hundred qing of good fields to the people of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the Linhan horse supervisor established in Yuanhe, turned thousands of horses over to government studs, and returned four hundred qing of good farmland to the people of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 頃之，固請老，不許。

translations.literal: Before long he firmly requested retirement; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked firmly to retire, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 八年，徙東都留守，俄加中書令。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to eastern capital regent, and soon made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 833 he was made regent of the eastern capital and soon appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李訓之禍，宦官肆威以逞，凡訓、注宗婭賓客悉收逮，訊報苛慘。

translations.literal: After Li Xun's calamity, eunuchs unleashed their awesomeness to display themselves; all guests and relatives of Xun and Zheng's clans were seized and arrested, and interrogation reports were harsh and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xun's disaster the eunuchs unleashed their power. All relatives and clients of Li Xun and Zheng Zhu were arrested, and interrogations were brutally harsh.

sentences.zh: 度上疏申理，全活數十姓。

translations.literal: Du sent up a memorial explaining and setting right matters, fully preserving the lives of several tens of clans.
translations.idiomatic: Du memorialized in their defense and saved dozens of families.

sentences.zh: 武德縣主藏史盜錢亡命，捕不得。

translations.literal: The Wude county chief repository clerk stole money and fled for his life; he could not be captured.
translations.idiomatic: A Wude county treasury clerk stole money and fled. He could not be captured.

sentences.zh: 河陽節度使溫造獄其令王賞責負，系三年，母死弗許喪。

translations.literal: Heyang military commissioner Wen Zao imprisoned his magistrate Wang Shang to make him responsible for the debt, detained him three years, and when his mother died did not permit mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Heyang commissioner Wen Zao imprisoned his magistrate Wang Shang over the debt, held him three years, and refused him mourning leave when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 度為帝言之，賞得釋。

translations.literal: Du spoke of it to the emperor, and Shang was released.
translations.idiomatic: Du told the emperor, and Wang Shang was released.

sentences.zh: 時閹豎擅威，天子擁虛器，搢紳道喪，度不復有經濟意，乃治第東都集賢裏，沼石林叢，岑繚幽勝。

translations.literal: At that time castrated attendants monopolized power, the Son of Heaven held an empty vessel, and the way of gentry was lost; Du no longer had intent for statecraft, and therefore built a residence in Jixian Ward of the eastern capital—marsh, stone, and forest thick, peaks winding in secluded beauty.
