translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs monopolized power, the emperor held only an empty throne, and official integrity was dead. Du no longer cared for statecraft. He built a mansion in Jixian Ward of Luoyang amid marshes, stones, and forests in secluded splendor.

sentences.zh: 午橋作別墅，具燠館涼臺，號「綠野堂」，激波其下。

translations.literal: At Wuqiao he made a villa, furnished with warm lodges and cool terraces, called "Green Wild Hall," with rushing waves below.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuqiao he built a villa with warm lodges and cool terraces called Green Wild Hall, with rushing water below.

sentences.zh: 度野服蕭散，與白居易、劉禹錫為文章、把酒，窮晝夜相歡，不問人間事。

translations.literal: Du in rustic dress was easy and unhurried; with Bai Juyi and Liu Yuxi he composed literature and raised cups, rejoicing together through day and night, not asking after worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Du dressed simply and lived at ease, writing and drinking with Bai Juyi and Liu Yuxi day and night, heedless of public affairs.

sentences.zh: 而帝知度年雖及，神明不衰，每大臣自洛來，必問度安否。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor knew that though Du's years had arrived, his spirit was not declining; whenever a chief minister came from Luo, he was sure to ask whether Du was safe and well.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor knew that though Du was aged, his mind remained sharp. Whenever a minister came from Luoyang, he asked after Du's health.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，復以本官節度河東。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he again took his existing office as military commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In 837 he was again made military commissioner of Hedong in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 度牢辭老疾，帝命吏部郎中盧弘宣諭意曰：「為朕臥護北門可也。

translations.literal: Du firmly declined on grounds of age and illness; the emperor ordered Ministry of Personnel bureau director Lu Hongxuan to convey his intent: "Lie and guard the northern gate for me—that will do."
translations.idiomatic: Du firmly declined on grounds of age and illness. The emperor sent Lu Hongxuan of the Ministry of Personnel to say, "Guard the northern gate for me from your bed if need be."

sentences.zh: 」趣上道，度乃之鎮。

translations.literal: He urged him onto the road; Du thereupon went to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Du was urged to depart at once and went to his post.

sentences.zh: 易定節度使張璠卒，軍中將立其子元益，度乃遣使曉譬禍福，元益懼，束身歸朝。

translations.literal: When Yiding military commissioner Zhang Fan died, the army wished to establish his son Yuanyi; Du sent envoys to explain prosperity and calamity, Yuanyi was afraid, bound himself, and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiding commissioner Zhang Fan died, the army wished to install his son Yuanyi. Du sent envoys to explain the consequences. Yuanyi was terrified and surrendered himself to the court.

sentences.zh: 三年，以病丐還東都。

translations.literal: In the third year, on grounds of illness he begged to return to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 838, ill, he begged to return to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 真拜中書令，臥家未克謝，有詔先給俸料。

translations.literal: He was truly appointed Director of the Secretariat; lying at home he could not yet offer thanks, and an edict first granted his salary provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He was formally appointed Director of the Secretariat but was too ill to attend court. The emperor ordered his salary paid in advance.

sentences.zh: 上巳宴群臣曲江，度不赴，帝賜詩曰：「注想待元老，識君恨不早。

translations.literal: On the shangsi festival he feasted the ministers at Qujiang; Du did not attend. The emperor bestowed a poem saying: "I fix my thoughts awaiting the elder statesman; knowing you, I regret it was not earlier.
translations.idiomatic: At the shangsi festival the emperor feasted his ministers at Qujiang. Du could not attend. The emperor sent a poem: "I have long awaited the elder statesman and regret knowing you so late.

sentences.zh: 我家柱石衰，憂來學丘禱。

translations.literal: My house's pillar and stone decline; worry comes and I study Qiu's prayers."
translations.idiomatic: The pillar of my house is failing. In my worry I pray as did Confucius."

sentences.zh: 」別詔曰：「方春慎疾為難，勉醫藥自持。

translations.literal: A separate edict said: "It is spring—being careful of illness is difficult; strive with medicine to sustain yourself.
translations.idiomatic: A separate edict said, "Spring makes illness hard to bear. Take your medicines and take care.

sentences.zh: 朕集中欲見公詩，故示此，異日可進。

translations.literal: In my collected works I wish to see your poems; therefore I show this—you may present them another day."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to include your poems in my collection and show you this one now. Send me more when you can."

sentences.zh: 」使者及門而度薨，年七十六。

translations.literal: When the envoy reached the gate, Du had died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reached his gate just as Du died, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 帝聞震悼，以詩置靈幾。

translations.literal: Hearing it, the emperor was shaken and grieved, and placed the poem on the spirit table.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stricken with grief and placed the poem on the mourning bier.

sentences.zh: 冊贈太傅，諡文忠，賵禮優縟，命京兆尹鄭復護喪。

translations.literal: By patent he was posthumously made Grand Tutor, posthumous name Wenzong, funeral gifts lavish and detailed; Capital Metropolis Intendant Zheng Fu was ordered to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Wenzong. Funeral gifts were lavish, and Capital Intendant Zheng Fu was ordered to oversee the rites.

sentences.zh: 度臨終，自為銘志。

translations.literal: At the end Du himself composed his inscription and record.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Du composed his own epitaph.

sentences.zh: 帝怪無遺奏，敕家人索之，得半槁，以儲貳為請，無私言。

translations.literal: The emperor wondered there was no final memorial and ordered the family to search; they obtained a half-draft asking for the heir apparent, with no private words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wondered that he left no final memorial and ordered his family to search. They found a half-finished draft asking only that the heir apparent be secured, with no private requests.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年，加贈太師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huichang he was further posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In 841 he was further posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 大中初，詔配享憲宗廟廷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong an edict ordered him enshrined in Emperor Xianzong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong reign he was ordered enshrined in Emperor Xianzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 度退然，才中人，而神觀邁爽，操守堅正，善占對。

translations.literal: Du was retiring and modest; talent was middling, yet his spirit and bearing were surpassing and bright, his conduct firm and upright, and he was skilled in responsive address.
translations.idiomatic: Du was modest and unassuming. His talent was middling, but his bearing was luminous, his integrity firm, and he excelled in debate.

sentences.zh: 既有功，名震四夷。

translations.literal: Once he had achievement, his name shook the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had won his victories, his name resounded among the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 使外國者，其君長必問度年今幾、狀貌孰似、天子用否。

translations.literal: Envoys to foreign states: their rulers were sure to ask Du's age now, whose appearance he most resembled, and whether the Son of Heaven employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys to foreign courts reported that foreign rulers always asked Du's age, whom he resembled, and whether the Son of Heaven still employed him.

sentences.zh: 其威譽德業比郭汾陽，而用不用常為天下重輕。

translations.literal: His awesomeness, reputation, virtue, and achievement were compared to Guo Ziyi of Fenyang, and whether he was used or not often made the realm heavy or light.
translations.idiomatic: His prestige and achievement were compared to Guo Ziyi of Fenyang, and whether he held office often weighed on the fortunes of the realm.

sentences.zh: 事四朝，以全德始終。

translations.literal: He served four reigns, with complete virtue from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: He served four reigns and preserved his integrity to the end.

sentences.zh: 及歿，天下莫不思其風烈。

translations.literal: When he died, none under Heaven did not think of his wind and fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the realm mourned his noble spirit.

sentences.zh: 葬管城，逮今廟食。

translations.literal: He was buried at Guancheng; down to today he receives temple offerings.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Guancheng, where he is honored in temple rites to this day.

sentences.zh: 五子，識、諗知名。

translations.literal: He had five sons; Shi and Shen were well known.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons, of whom Shi and Shen were the best known.

sentences.zh: 子 識

translations.literal: Son: Shi
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi

sentences.zh: 識，字通理，性敏悟，凡經目未始忘。

translations.literal: Shi, taboo name Tongli, was by nature keen and perceptive; whatever passed his eyes he never forgot.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, styled Tongli, was quick-witted and never forgot anything he read.

sentences.zh: 推廕補京兆參軍，擢累大理少卿。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he was supplemented as staff officer of the capital metropolis, was selected and repeatedly promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered service as a Capital staff officer and rose to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 王師討劉稹，為供軍使。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Liu Zhen, he was supply commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the court campaigned against Liu Zhen, he served as army supply commissioner.

sentences.zh: 稹平，改司農卿，進湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: When Zhen was pacified, he was changed to Minister of Agriculture and advanced to Hunan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhen fell he was made Minister of Agriculture, then Hunan governor.

sentences.zh: 入拜大理卿，襲晉國公半封。

translations.literal: He entered court as chief of the Court of Judicial Review and inherited half the enfeoffment of Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as chief of the Court of Judicial Review and inherited half his father's enfeoffment as Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 為涇原節度使。

translations.literal: He was made military commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 時蕃酋尚恐熱上三州七關，列屯分守。

translations.literal: At that time the Tibetan chieftain Shang Kongre presented the three prefectures and seven passes; they set up camps in array to guard separately.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan chieftain Shang Kongre had surrendered three prefectures and seven passes, which were garrisoned in separate camps.

sentences.zh: 宣宗擇名臣，以識帥涇原，畢諴帥邠甯，李福帥夏州，帝親臨遣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong chose renowned ministers: Shi to command Jingyuan, Bi Dan to command Bin-Ning, Li Fu to command Xiazhou—the emperor personally saw them off on dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong chose renowned ministers: Shi for Jingyuan, Bi Dan for Bin-Ning, and Li Fu for Xiazhou, and saw them off in person.

sentences.zh: 識至，治堡障，整戎器，開屯田。

translations.literal: When Shi arrived, he repaired fortifications, put in order weapons, and opened military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Shi repaired fortifications, reorganized weapons, and opened military colonies.

sentences.zh: 初，將士守邊，或積歲不得還。

translations.literal: At first soldiers guarding the border sometimes could not return for accumulated years.
translations.idiomatic: Previously border troops sometimes served for years without rotation.

sentences.zh: 識與立戍限，滿者代；

translations.literal: Shi with them established garrison limits—when full, replace;
translations.idiomatic: Shi set terms of service: when a tour was complete, men were replaced;

sentences.zh: 親七十，近戍。

translations.literal: if parents were seventy, garrison nearby.
translations.idiomatic: if a soldier's parents were seventy, he was posted nearby.

sentences.zh: 由是人感悅。

translations.literal: From this the men were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 加檢校刑部尚書，徙鳳翔、忠武、天平、邠甯、靈武等軍。

translations.literal: He was made acting Minister of Justice and transferred through the armies of Fengxiang, Zhongwu, Tianping, Bin-Ning, Lingwu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Minister of Justice and served in turn at Fengxiang, Zhongwu, Tianping, Bin-Ning, Lingwu, and other commands.

sentences.zh: 進檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was advanced to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 靈武地斥鹵無井，識誓神而鑿之，果得泉。

translations.literal: Lingwu's land was saline without wells; Shi vowed to the spirits and drilled, and indeed obtained a spring.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwu's land was brackish and without wells. Shi vowed to the spirits, drilled, and found a spring.

sentences.zh: 曆六節度，所蒞皆有可述。

translations.literal: He passed through six military commissions; wherever he presided there was something to recount.
translations.idiomatic: He held six military commissions, and in each left accomplishments worth recounting.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空，諡曰昭。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works, posthumous name Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works with the posthumous name Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子 諗

translations.literal: Son: Shen
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen

sentences.zh: 諗有文，籍廕累官考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Shen had literary talent; through registry privilege he accumulated offices to outer vice director of the Ministry of Personnel for merit evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was a gifted writer who rose through privilege to outer vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宣宗訪元和宰相子，思度勳望，故待諗有加。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong inquired after the sons of Yuanhe chief ministers, thought of Du's merit and stature, and therefore treated Shen with extra favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong inquired after the sons of Yuanhe chief ministers and, remembering Du's merit, treated Shen with special favor.

sentences.zh: 為翰林學士，累遷工部侍郎，詔加承旨。

translations.literal: He was made Hanlin academician, was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of public works, and by edict was made chief academician.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Hanlin academician, rose to vice minister of public works, and was made chief academician by edict.

sentences.zh: 適會帝幸其院，諗即稱謝。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor visited his institute; Shen at once offered thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Hanlin institute, Shen thanked him at once.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「可歸與妻子相慶。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You may return and celebrate with wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Go home and celebrate with your wife and children."

sentences.zh: 」取禦奩果以賜，諗舉衣跽受。

translations.literal: He took imperial casket fruit to bestow; Shen raised his robe and knelt to receive.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him fruit from the imperial casket. Shen knelt and received it with both hands.

sentences.zh: 帝顧宮人取巾裹賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor turned to palace women to take a cloth wrapper and bestow it on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had a palace woman bring a cloth wrapper for the gift.

sentences.zh: 後為太子少師，封河東郡公。

translations.literal: Later he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 黃巢盜國，迫以偽官，不從，遇害。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao usurped the state, he was compelled with a false office; he did not obey and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao seized power, Shen was offered a rebel post. He refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：憲宗討蔡，出入四年。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Xianzong's campaign against Cai went in and out for four years.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Emperor Xianzong's campaign against Cai lasted four years from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 元濟外連奸臣，刺宰相及用事者，沮駭朝謀。

translations.literal: Yuanji externally linked with treacherous ministers, assassinated chief ministers and those in power, and frustrated and terrified court plans.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji allied with treacherous ministers at court, had chief ministers and power-holders assassinated, and paralyzed the throne's strategy.

sentences.zh: 惟天子赫然排群議，任度政事，倚以討賊。

translations.literal: Only the Son of Heaven awesomely brushed aside the multitude of opinions, entrusted Du with government affairs, and relied on him to campaign against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Only the emperor boldly overrode the multitude of counsels, entrusted Du with government, and relied on him to crush the rebels.

sentences.zh: 身督戰，遂平淮西。

translations.literal: He personally supervised the campaign and thereby pacified Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: Du took command in person and pacified Huai West.

sentences.zh: 非度破賊之難，任度之為難也。

translations.literal: It was not Du's breaking the rebels that was difficult—it was entrusting Du that was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The hard part was not defeating the rebels but entrusting Du to do it.

sentences.zh: 韓愈頌其功曰：「凡此蔡功，惟斷乃成。

translations.literal: Han Yu praised his achievement, saying: "All this achievement over Cai was accomplished only through resolute decision."
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu praised his achievement in verse: "All this victory over Cai was won only through resolute decision."

sentences.zh: 」其知言哉！

translations.literal: How well he spoke!
translations.idiomatic: How rightly he spoke!

sentences.zh: 穆宗不君，憸人腐夫乘釁鐫詆，而度遂無顯功。

translations.literal: Muzong did not rule as a true sovereign; treacherous men and rotten fellows seized the opening to carve and slander, and Du therefore had no conspicuous achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong did not rule as a true sovereign. Treacherous and corrupt men seized their chance to slander Du, and he won no further conspicuous victories.

sentences.zh: 非前智後愚，用不用，勢當然矣。

translations.literal: It was not wisdom before and folly after, or use and non-use—the momentum was necessarily so.
translations.idiomatic: This was not wisdom in one reign and folly in another, nor use versus neglect—it was simply the way circumstances had to be.

sentences.zh: 前史稱度晚節頗浮沉為自安計，是不然。

translations.literal: Earlier histories say Du's later years were rather adrift and floating as a plan for self-preservation—that is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories say Du's later years were marked by drift and self-preservation. That is not so.

sentences.zh: 《大雅》曰：「既明且哲，以保其身。

translations.literal: The Greater Odes say: "Both bright and wise, thereby preserving one's person."
translations.idiomatic: The Greater Odes say, "Bright and wise, he thereby preserved himself."
